title: Greek trade unions prepare for nationwide general strike on November 25
seoTitle: Athens protest for nationwide general strike

tea.why: Protesters oppose policies affecting incomes and rights, high living costs, and state involvement in military conflicts.
tea.want: Demanding substantial wage increases, collective bargaining agreements, lower taxes on fuel and electricity, and staff recruitment.
tea.changed: Nov 8: Unions and worker federations across Greece continued preparations and announced rally locations for the upcoming general strike.

summary: Greek trade unions, public sector employees represented by ADEDY, regional associations, and numerous labor centers are preparing for a nationwide general strike scheduled for November 25, 2026. Organizers and primary unions are demanding substantial wage increases, the reintroduction of the 13th and 14th salary, collective bargaining agreements, lower taxation on essential goods, and an end to military spending and foreign interventions. Rallies are planned in multiple cities, including Athens at Propylaea, Thessaloniki, and Piraeus. The mobilization follows a series of sector-specific protests and assemblies held across the country.
demands: Abolition of taxes on fuel, electricity, and VAT on staple foods
Hiring of personnel and permanent status for contract workers
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: The Athens Labor Center held a joint meeting with trade unions to organize the upcoming strike demands.
An educational rally took place with participation from teachers, student associations, and pupils.
Trade unions and worker associations issued announcements detailing locations and times for the November 25 strike.
